newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Egypt's leader could meet Netanyahu after Hebron.
newsitem.headline: Egypt's leader could meet Netanyahu after Hebron.

text.p: Egypt's leader Hosni Mubarak is ready to meet Israel's Benjamin Netanyahu once Israel completes the long-delayed handover of most of Hebron to Palestinian rule, Egypt's foreign minister said on Tuesday.

President Mubarak has refused to see Prime Minister Netanyahu until Israel and the PLO agree. The handover of the West Bank town has been delayed for 10 months by security concerns, violence and a change of government in Israel in June.
Asked if Mubarak would meet Netanyahu again, Foreign Minister Amr Moussa told Israel Radio's English service by telephone: "Once it's signed and implemented, absolutely. We have nothing against that.

"In fact if the prime minister wants to come to visit Egypt and to talk to the president and to have a discussion about the peace process, I believe he would be more than welcome," Moussa told the radio.
Mubarak and Netanyahu's last and only meeting was in July in Cairo.

Egypt and Jordan -- both parties to peace treaties with Israel -- broke an earlier deadlock on Sunday with a compromise proposal for Israel to complete other West Bank redeployments after Hebron. The date is now expected to be mid-1998.
Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat scheduled a midnight meeting at their border to try to nail down a Hebron deal.
